stemMd: According to the passage, why was a timetable in each station's local time particularly dangerous on single-track lines?
instructionsMd: Answer on the basis of the passage only.

options.label: A
options.textMd: The time at a company's headquarters differed from the time in the capital.

options.label: B
options.textMd: Trains travelling towards each other had to be kept apart by the timetable alone.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Passengers could not tell which train they were meant to board.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Station clocks could not show two different times at once.

explanationMd:
The second paragraph gives the reason in one clause: single-track lines are those "where two trains travelling towards each other had to be kept apart by the timetable alone". If the timetable is written in a different time at every station, the schedule that is supposed to keep the trains apart is itself inconsistent.

**How to check.** The sentence separates two problems: local times were "confusing to passengers" and, "more seriously, dangerous" on single-track lines. The question asks about the danger, and the passage attaches only one explanation to it.

distractorRationale.c: Passenger confusion is the passage's FIRST, lesser problem. The danger on single-track lines is a separate point, about keeping opposing trains apart.
distractorRationale.d: The passage says the reverse: station clocks sometimes showed railway time "alongside the local time", so displaying two times was possible.
distractorRationale.a: The passage mentions headquarters and capital time only as alternative choices of reference time. It never says they differed, or that this caused danger.

accessibilityText: A question about the passage on railway time. It asks why local-time timetables were particularly dangerous on single-track lines. The options are: opposing trains had to be kept apart by the timetable alone; passengers could not tell which train to board; station clocks could not show two times; headquarters time differed from capital time.

provenance.notes: Original explicit-information item. Distractors are the lesser problem the same sentence names, a reversed detail, and an unstated comparison.
